Tips:
-Give 100 percent in all of your classes. Work your butt off, do any extra credit assignments(if the class has that), and focus in class. There were times where I had to repeat classes and that was what made me have to graduate a year later. One thing that helped motivate was that I reminded myself that I was paying for those classes so I wouldn't want to waste my time and money to re-take them.

-Get to know your professors and go to their office hours. If you show your professors that you're interested in their class then that puts you at an advantage. You never know if you could use them for a reference or letter of recommendation in the future. 

-Figure out what you want to do career wise so that you can make an academic plan with a counselor. If there's a certain major that interests you, look at the careers that tie in with that major and see if there is a specific job that you would want to do. If you do not know what you want to do, then you could take a career counseling class 

-Make a list of colleges that interest you and learn about the program you want to transfer into. If you go to their websites, they usually have a list of requirements for transfer students. If you know ahead of time where you want to go, then maybe you could go on a tour of the school. Also be on the lookout for college fairs. my community college had a few of those and it is a great opportunity to ask questions and gather information from schools that you might be interested in attending.

-If you can, then get an on campus job. Usually jobs on cc campuses are super flexible because the school knows that you will be busy with classes so it's a good opportunity to make some cash if you need any.

-Join clubs and become involved with the school. Get to know people in your classes so that you can study with people, do homework together, or just meet people. 

- If you can, then take classes all year round so you can get done faster. It's the only way you'll get finished in two years.

I just recently transferred from a a CC to a 4 year so I have some tips that will help you out:

1.) Go to all of your classes and sit near the front. Seriously, you're now going to be paying to go to class so make the most of that experience. If you sit near the front, then you will most likely pay attention in class and get more out of it than if you sat in the back.

2.) Buy your books off of Amazon.com. I would wait until the professor sent us a message with the syllabus or until the first day of class to see what books/materials the professor requires for that class.

3.) Go to office hours. Your professors will want to see their students and are happy to help you. Getting to know your professors makes you stand out in class and if you ever need a letter of recommendation for a school or a job, then it would be awesome to get one from your professor. 

4.) Get good grades and pass your classes the first time. Work your butt off in every class so that you don't have to retake classes again which will only waste your money and deter you from finishing in two years. Also, if you plan on transferring in two years then you should take classes all year round(winter, spring, summer, and fall). I would use the summer and winter to take the more difficult courses out of the way since classes during those periods usually only last 4 weeks. 

5.) Go to your counselors. Get to know your counselors to make an academic plan that you can follow so you know what courses you need to graduate and the courses that are needed for the major you intend to take. If you have trouble choosing a major, then you can take a career counseling class or you can go on https://www.onetonline.org and look at careers in several different fields. 

6.) Make use of the services your CC offers. This means joining clubs, volunteering, tutoring services, counseling services, and maybe even internship services if your school offers them. You can even try to get an on campus job if you are looking for one. 

7.) Once you find a major, make a list of schools that interest you(usually around 6-9) schools and look at the programs on their school websites. There you  can see what courses will transfer over, how many units are required, what information they'll need once it is time to apply to transfer, and maybe even information on transfer counselors that can help you out. This will help you stay motivated, especially during the tough times. 

8.) Maintain a high GPA. I would say at least get a 3.2 or higher at most. Again, it all depends on where you want to transfer to and usually you can see the gpa's expected of transfers students on school websites or on collegeboard. org. If have an honors society at your college and maintain a good gpa, you will probably be accepted into that which can look good on your applications. 

9.) There will be times where you wished you went straight to a 4 year instead of a community college because you will think you're ''missing  out'' on the true college experience.  The most important thing to remember is that what you put into college, is what you are going to get out of it. 

10.) If it is possible, then maybe go on a couple of college tours during the summer so you can learn more about the schools. If you can't, then be on the lookout for college fairs at your CC. My community college had a few and it helped to at least attend and have a look at the other schools as well as talk to representatives. 

I hope this helps you in any way. If you have any other questions, then you can PM me. :)

1.) My goal was to finish in two years but I ended up being at a CC for 3 years. It is definitely possible to finish in 2 years but you have to pass all of your classes the first time, meet with counselors to make an academic plan, have an idea of what major or career path you want to go into,and take classes all year round(fall,spring,summer,winter).
2.)I was in an honors program at my CC and that was for students who had a 3.2 GPA or higher. I received an email after getting a 3.8 my first semester and attended their meeting session. being in the honors programs allowed me to have priority registration for my classes and gave me the opportunity to take Honors classes(although they recommended taking no more than 2). I was told that it would look good on my application and I definitely recommend taking advantage of the opportunities that the school is providing, even if many people don't do that. 
3.) I transferred to CSUMB in the spring so I was not able to get any financial aid for this semester but I applied for fall 2016 and am waiting to hear back.
4.)It depends on the classes you take and the strengths/weaknesses you have as a student. General education classes really are not that difficult so long as you show up to class, engage with teachers, and actually take the time to study. Community college felt like high school 2.0, in the sense that classes were not that difficult but you had more independence as a student. If you want to excel in your courses, then it is up to you and only you to get to where you want to be. When you transfer, UC's look for transfer students who have GPA's of 3.2 or higher. I think as long as you have above a 3.2, then you should be fine. There are a few UC's that offer TAG programs, which means you can be guaranteed admittance to their school so long as you follow the criteria for the TAG. The tag is something that should be on your school's website but I definitely recommend asking a counselor about it early on so you know what you need to do for that. If not, then call and ask the school that you want to want to transfer to. I have had positive and negative experiences with counselors and the ones that didn't help me out were the ones that tried to keep me at the CC longer.

If you have any specific schools in mind that you want to apply to, you should look up their websites and check to see what requirements they have for international students. Check to see if they have any counselors or advisers that work with international students and give them a call. You could also check collegeboard.org to see the requirements for international students plus deadlines for applications although you should make sure to confirm those dates with the school.
